Subject: Post-demo recap + next steps: SDK, auth, and dedicated sizing

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our demo and the ops items we discussed; I pulled the key asks together so we can get you a committed plan this week: 

1) SDK + auth starter
   - We’ll send a small repo with sample integration using our Node + Python SDKs and an auth pattern for enterprise (API key + short-lived tokens).
   - Action: NovaHealth to confirm preferred auth (API keys vs OIDC/SSO + SCIM).

2) Routing and environments
   - You mentioned staging in us-west and production in us-east — we’ll recommend region pinning + failover routing.

3) Structured output & tool calling
   - For the clinical extraction use-case you showed, we’ll provide a tool-calling example (structured JSON + schema validation).

4) Embeddings / reranker plan
   - Proposal: batch embed nightly for the knowledge corpus (approx 15k docs initially) + realtime reranking for top-k candidates.

5) Dedicated capacity sizing (initial ask)
   - Please confirm expected concurrent user sessions and peak requests per second (RPS). Our initial sizing asks: 200 peak RPS, avg request size ~750 tokens, targeting 95th pct latency <= 250ms for generation-only requests.
   - Autoscale: target policy suggestions below once we confirm traffic profile.

Attachments: proposed-sizing.xlsx (initial numbers), mutual-action-plan.md (Drive link included below).

Next step: if you confirm the concurrency/RPS and auth preference, we can return a committed Dedicated capacity configuration and a draft SOW for procurement.

Available for a short follow-up Tuesday morning PT — what works for you?

Best,
Logan

Hi Logan —

Appreciate the recap. Quick answers and context from our side: 

- Auth: we need enterprise SSO (OIDC) with SCIM provisioning; API keys only acceptable for prototype.
- Peak: preliminary internal estimate is ~120 concurrent active users, peak burst up to ~180 RPS for short windows (3–5 minutes).
- Typical prompt sizes vary; average inbound text ~500 tokens but extraction + follow-ups can reach ~1400 tokens.
- Embeddings: batch nightly looks right; we want 768-d vectors (current infra).
- Compliance: we’ll send a short security questionnaire (attached) — we need to confirm data residency and retention options.

Procurement: procurement@novahealth.com has requested a timeline for a signed SOW within the next 3 weeks if numbers look good.

Can you call out autoscale gating criteria (CPU/GPU queue depth, token/sec) in the follow up? Also need SLA tiers (Gold vs Standard) and any credit policy for downtime.

Thanks,

Looping in a few clarifying technical questions we should get resolved before we finalize the Dedicated config: 

- Can NovaHealth share a percentile distribution for prompt + response token lengths (P50/P90/P99)? We need this to estimate KV cache hit rates and memory needs.
- Are reranker queries latency-sensitive (<=100ms) or can they tolerate 200–300ms? That determines whether we colocate rerankers on generation nodes or use a dedicated CPU pool.
- Embedding vector dim 768 confirmed — what QPS for semantic search lookups (per user)?

Ben — can you draft a candidate autoscale policy (metrics + thresholds) and recommended queue depth / concurrency per worker for the numbers Emily provided? I’ll assemble into the sizing workbook.

Thanks,
Karthik

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + next steps: SDK, auth, and dedicated sizing

Hi all —

Quick technical notes and a candidate runtime config attached (sample stub). High-level recommendations given NovaHealth’s burst to ~180 RPS and token sizes: 

- Worker concurrency: aim for 8–12 concurrent generation streams per GPU worker for 1xA10-like instance; tune after a short soak.
- Queueing: soft queue depth 400 requests (ingress), with a hard backpressure cutoff at 1,200 requests to protect KV cache eviction churn.
- Autoscale triggers (candidate): 
   * Scale-out: GPU utilization > 70% for >60s OR average queue depth per cluster > 250 for >45s.
   * Scale-in: GPU utilization < 35% for >120s AND queue depth < 100 for >90s.
- Batching: enable continuous batching with a 40ms max batch wait to hit high throughput while keeping tail latency low.
- KV caching: pin frequent prompt prefixes (clinical templates) to keep warm; expect ~35–45% token cost savings for repeated flows.
- Reranker placement: if latency target <=100ms, put reranker on generation node as a colocation microservice; otherwise route to CPU-only pool for cost efficiency.

I attached runtime-config-sample.json (small stub) and will drop a one-page sunk-cost estimate into the sizing spreadsheet.

Next step: Logan — if NovaHealth confirms auth and the final RPS/concurrency number, we’ll convert this into a committed Dedicated config and SOW draft for procurement.

Ben Carter
